records.source: 字源 (李學勤主編; 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692)
records.field: PDF p. 87; printed p. 75; headword entry and scan-verified passage
records.text: The scan shows the headword 口 and its reading note. The entry calls it a pictograph shaped like a human mouth, says its basic meaning is ‘mouth’, cites an oracle-bone occurrence and the poem 詩·豳風·鴟鴞 using 口 in its basic sense, and notes that bronze inscriptions also use it as a clan sign. It describes ancient forms as generally two strokes and says three-stroke writing may appear by Han times, with stroke order differing from modern practice. I inspected the original scan pixels for the headword, forms, cited lines, and the entry’s ending before 囑. The account supports the mouth pictograph; the stroke-history statement is the book’s proposal, not independently confirmed here.
